**Assessment of the three proposed answers**

**Path lower bound (holds for all p).** On a path, every interior vertex has degree 2, and the minimizer of |x−a|^p + |x−b|^p is the midpoint (a+b)/2 for every p>1. So the dynamics is the same as the p=2 random Gauss–Seidel iteration. Its mean error decays at rate about 1/n³ per step, so τ ≳ n³ log(1/ε) and β_p ≥ 3 for every p. Any answer below 3 on (1,3) is therefore wrong.

**Solution 3 (p+1)** is ruled out. For p<2, p+1<3, which violates the path lower bound. Its Bregman/PL argument also assumes a uniform edge-weight factor, which cancels in the diagonal-scaled rate, so the n^{p+1} scaling does not follow.

**Solution 2 (3)** is consistent with the path bound, but it claims the complete graph never beats the path for p<2. That ignores the nonlinearity. I checked the flat mode on K_n with boundary values 0 and 1 and interior values near 1/2. Writing the interior deviation as ε, the single-vertex update moves by η ~ (ε/n)^{1/(p−1)}, so the mean moves by about ε^{1/(p−1)} n^{−p/(p−1)} per step. Integrating gives τ ~ n^{p/(p−1)} ε^{−(2−p)/(p−1)}. This is consistent with the linear case at p=2 (n², below the path's n³), and it exceeds n³ when p<3/2. So a constant 3 cannot be right for p near 1. The problem's phrasing, "explicit function of p", also points away from a constant.

**Solution 1 (max(3, p/(p−1)))** is the only answer whose lower bound I could verify. The K_n mean-field computation supports the p/(p−1) term for p<3/2, and the path supports the 3. I have not verified the upper bound for every graph, nor the behaviour on (2,3), where the answer may differ from 3. Its matching upper-bound argument is only sketched, so this is a best-supported choice rather than a confirmed one.

CHOICE: 1
